title: Web framework: middleware, AOP and async
description: Servlet filters, interceptors, AOP and FastAPI middleware/dependencies, plus async endpoints, streaming and server-sent events in both stacks.
source: Spring Framework AOP and MVC docs; Servlet specification; Starlette middleware docs; FastAPI docs (middleware, concurrency and async/await, custom response); AnyIO thread limiter docs; Project Reactor docs; Baeldung
seriesDescription: Topic-by-topic JEE-style quizzes for the backend and AI-engineering interview roadmap: integer, assertion-reason, matrix match, fill-in-the-blanks, short code writing, plus multi-correct questions. Language core, concurrency, DSA, web frameworks, data access, databases, messaging, resilience, security, testing, system design, LLM and agent engineering.

questions.prompt: Match each Spring mechanism with the job it is best suited for.

right.text: Wrap the raw request/response before DispatcherServlet, e.g. token parsing or request-id logging
Use the resolved handler method in preHandle/postHandle, e.g. per-controller auth checks
Time or audit calls to service-bean methods, even outside HTTP
Translate exceptions from any controller into a uniform error body

questions.explanation: Filters are Servlet-container level, interceptors are Spring MVC level (they know the handler), aspects are proxy-based and work on any Spring bean, and advice classes handle exceptions.

questions.prompt: Three Starlette middleware A, B and C are added to an app in that order with app.add_middleware(A), then B, then C. At which position (1 = first to see an incoming request) does A's pre-request code run?
questions.explanation: Middleware added last is outermost, so a request goes C, B, A. Responses unwind A, B, C. Verified with @app.middleware logging.

questions.text: {1} runs before the handler and can stop the chain by returning false; {2} runs after the handler but before the view is rendered; {3} runs after the request completes, even when the handler threw.
questions.explanation: doFilter belongs to Servlet filters and afterReturning to AOP advice. postHandle is skipped when the handler throws, afterCompletion is not.

questions.prompt: Write a Spring aspect class TimingAspect (a bean) with an @Around advice that times every method of classes in package com.acme.service and its sub-packages, then returns the real result.

checks.label: uses @Around with an execution pointcut on com.acme.service
calls proceed() and returns its result
measures time with nanoTime or currentTimeMillis

questions.explanation: Forgetting proceed() silently swallows the call. Needs spring-boot-starter-aop in Boot 3 (renamed spring-boot-starter-aspectj in Boot 4). Pointcuts using within() or an annotation are valid alternatives.

questions.prompt: Write a FastAPI HTTP middleware that measures how long the request took (time.perf_counter) and sets the response header X-Process-Time.
questions.model:
@app.middleware("http")
async def add_time(request, call_next):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["X-Process-Time"] = str(time.perf_counter() - start)
    return response
questions.explanation: Pure ASGI middleware or add_middleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware) subclasses are equivalent. Note BaseHTTPMiddleware has caveats with streaming responses and contextvars.

questions.prompt: Write a FastAPI dependency require_key that reads the X-API-Key header and raises HTTPException 401 unless it equals "secret", then attach it to a router so every route needs it.
questions.starter: from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Header, HTTPException
questions.explanation: Dependencies are the FastAPI answer to per-route auth: they run inside routing, know path params and can use other dependencies. Verified: missing header gives 422, wrong key 401, right key 200.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: Spring AOP advice does not run when a bean calls one of its own advised methods via this.
questions.reason: Spring AOP is proxy-based, and an internal call bypasses the proxy.

whys.a: Correct: the call never leaves the target object, so the proxy that applies advice is skipped.

questions.explanation: Same root cause as @Transactional self-invocation. Fixes: refactor into another bean, inject the proxy, or use AspectJ weaving.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: A Servlet filter that never calls chain.doFilter(request, response) stops the request from reaching the controller.
questions.reason: Filters can be ordered with @Order or a FilterRegistrationBean.

whys.a: Wrong: ordering does not explain why the request stops.
whys.b: Correct: both true; the chain simply is not continued, and ordering is an unrelated fact.
whys.d: Wrong: A is true; a filter can also short-circuit with its own response.

questions.explanation: Auth filters use exactly this to return 401 early. Order matters: a security filter must run before a logging filter that reads the principal.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: A FastAPI dependency can short-circuit a request by raising HTTPException.
questions.reason: Dependencies run only after all middleware has already returned a response.

whys.c: Correct: A is true, but R is false because dependencies run inside route handling, i.e. within the middleware stack.

questions.explanation: Order: middleware (outer) then routing then dependencies then handler, and back out through middleware again.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: HandlerInterceptor.postHandle is called even when the controller method throws an exception.
questions.reason: afterCompletion is called after the handler finishes, including when it threw (provided preHandle returned true).

whys.d: Correct: postHandle is skipped on exceptions; afterCompletion is the callback for cleanup.

questions.explanation: Put resource cleanup and metrics in afterCompletion, not postHandle.

questions.prompt: An async def FastAPI endpoint calls time.sleep(2) inside its body. A single uvicorn worker receives 3 requests at the same instant. About how many seconds until the last client gets its response?
questions.explanation: time.sleep blocks the event loop, so requests are served one after another: 3 x 2 = 6. With a plain def the work runs in the threadpool, giving roughly 2, and await asyncio.sleep(2) also gives roughly 2.

questions.prompt: Your FastAPI endpoint calls a synchronous, blocking database driver. Which declaration is the safest choice?

options.text: A plain def endpoint, so FastAPI runs it in a threadpool.
options.why: The sync code runs off the event loop, so other requests keep flowing.

options.text: async def, with the blocking call made directly inside the endpoint body.
options.why: The blocking call freezes the whole event loop while it runs.

options.text: async def and sprinkle await in front of the driver call.
options.why: Awaiting a non-awaitable fails; it does not make the driver non-blocking.

options.text: async def plus a global asyncio lock.
options.why: A lock serialises requests and does not stop the loop from blocking.

questions.explanation: Use async def only with async libraries (asyncpg, httpx.AsyncClient) or offload with run_in_threadpool.

questions.prompt: Write a FastAPI GET /events endpoint that streams server-sent events: an async generator that yields "data: tick N" for N = 0, 1, 2 (with the SSE blank-line terminator), wrapped in a streaming response of the right media type.
questions.explanation:
Each SSE event ends with a blank line. Verified: output is 'data: 0

data: 1

' with content type text/event-stream. In Spring, return an SseEmitter or Flux<ServerSentEvent> with produces=TEXT_EVENT_STREAM_VALUE.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which statements about Spring async and WebFlux are correct?

options.text: @Async only takes effect when @EnableAsync is present and the call goes through the proxy.
options.why: Without both, the method runs synchronously on the caller's thread.

options.text: An @Async method may return void, Future or CompletableFuture.
options.why: Those are the supported return types; callers get the result through the future.

options.text: Mono<T> represents 0..1 elements and Flux<T> represents 0..N.
options.why: That is the core of Reactor's model.

options.text: A Mono does the work as soon as the method returns it, without subscription.
options.why: Reactive streams are lazy; nothing happens until subscribed (WebFlux subscribes for you).

options.text: An exception thrown in a void @Async method propagates to the caller.
options.why: It does not; it goes to an AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler.
Proxy-based advice cannot intercept private methods.

questions.explanation: WebFlux needs a non-blocking stack end to end; one blocking JDBC call on an event-loop thread hurts like time.sleep in async def. Virtual threads (Java 21) are the simple alternative.

questions.prompt: A plain def FastAPI endpoint runs time.sleep(1) in the default threadpool, which allows 40 worker threads. One uvicorn worker receives 100 requests at the same instant. About how many seconds until the last response?
questions.explanation: Sync endpoints run in AnyIO's threadpool with a default limit of 40 threads, so the 100 requests go in batches of 40, 40 and 20: 3 seconds (measured 3.3 s locally). The same 100 requests to an async def with asyncio.sleep(1) would take about 1 s.

questions.prompt: True or false: in FastAPI, when a dependency raises HTTPException(401), the resulting 401 response still passes back through your @app.middleware("http") function, so a header set there is added to it.

options.why: Correct: HTTPException is converted to a response by Starlette's exception handling, which sits inside user middleware.
The 401 is a normal response object by the time it unwinds, so middleware still sees it; only unhandled exceptions (500) bypass this.

questions.explanation: ExceptionMiddleware sits inside the middleware you add, so HTTPException responses unwind through it (verified locally: 401 carried the middleware's header). Truly unhandled exceptions are turned into 500 by the outermost ServerErrorMiddleware.
